explanation: General loss of excitatory drive or network gain: any manipulation that lowers regenerative excitation by a sufficient amount stops bursts in a network that sits near threshold; d-APV is then not NMDAR-specific evidence
what_it_predicts: Bursts abolished also by AMPA block, by a presynaptic release reduction or by another matched-effect manipulation; the burst falls steeply with a small change in total drive (threshold)
what_observed_fits_or_not: Fits: the knockout network is more excitable (RMP about 5.6 mV more depolarised, Rin 39 percent higher, sIPSC amplitude halved), the burst frequency is only about 0.8-2.3 per minute, and d-APV abolished the bursts. Cannot be separated from AB02/AB03 by d-APV alone; needs a matched-effect control that reduces non-NMDAR excitation to the same measured extent, read on at least two metrics and with a second receptor-agnostic release-reducing control, because a matched percent depends on the metric chosen

explanation: Carbenoxolone effect by block of NMDA receptors
what_it_predicts: If CBX blocks NMDAR directly, evoked NMDAR EPSC and the delayed field response fall under CBX; glutamate-evoked whole-cell NMDAR current falls with fast onset
what_observed_fits_or_not: Cited by the paper to a murine hippocampal LTP and NMDA study that was not reached here (no open full text; abstract not read). In the primary papers read: in autaptic hippocampal culture CBX at 100 uM reduced NMDAR EPSC to 69.1 +/- 3.2 percent with a higher paired-pulse ratio, consistent with a presynaptic site; direct glutamate-evoked currents were tested only with NMDAR blocked (AMPA component 95.7 percent), so a direct NMDAR channel block was not excluded or shown. In rat CA1 slices at P12 CBX 100 uM (bath and pipette) left the ischaemic inward current unchanged by test (mean about 2.1 nA vs about 2.7 nA control, 22 percent lower, P = 0.46, n = 6 vs 14, so an effect of the size Tovar found cannot be excluded); at P20 CBX was tested only together with La3+ (P = 0.43). That current is a reversed-uptake ischaemic glutamate current, not evoked vesicular release, so it neither contradicts Tovar nor excludes an NMDAR block. Unresolved
